title: Zephyrine and the Wolf
premise: Coral Delacroix poisons himself nightly so the Queen may eat safely, and by day he keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, which trades in souls, years, and names. When a prophecy written a century ago names him as the taster who will either save or doom the free cities, Coral learns his own soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain before he was born—the price of his family's survival. To reclaim it before the usurper's armies arrive, he must bargain with the wolf-god Zephyrine, who demands a terrible toll: every immunity Coral has built, surrendered at once. In the end Coral reclaims his soul but loses his protection, choosing to face death openly rather than survive by slow poison, and his choice breaks the prophecy's chain.
about_author: Wren Marchetti is a former apothecary's apprentice from the coastal town of Greyharbor who claims to have tasted everything once, on purpose. Zephyrine and the Wolf is their second novel, following the acclaimed The Ledger of Small Debts.

chapters.title: The Ninety-First Dish
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral tastes a suspect pheasant at the royal table, cataloguing its toxins with clinical calm while hiding his double life in the Guild's ledgers. Emotional beat: quiet dread—he realizes someone seasoned the dish specifically for him.

chapters.title: Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At the guildhall, Coral records the night's trades—a stolen shadow, three borrowed years—and finds an entry in his own handwriting dated before his birth: 'One soul, sold, court beneath the mountain.' Emotional beat: vertigo of self-estrangement.

chapters.title: The Prophecy of Ash
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A scholar-client pays the guild to authenticate a century-old prophecy naming 'the Taster' as savior or ruin of the free cities. The description matches Coral exactly, down to tonight's date. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The wolf-god, bound to the mountain road, scents Coral's half-sold soul and remembers the Delacroix debt. Emotional beat: ancient hunger tempered by unexpected curiosity about this small, poisoned man.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Herald
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The usurper's herald arrives demanding the guild's ledgers as tribute; the guildmaster refuses and is unmade into a name no one can remember. Emotional beat: grief and the first taste of real war.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Snowline
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Fleeing the city, Coral seeks Zephyrine and offers anything for passage to the mountain court. The wolf names his price: all ninety-one immunities, surrendered when the soul is reclaimed. Emotional beat: desperate hope priced in agony.

chapters.title: The Road That Eats Names
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Coral and Zephyrine travel the old wolf-road, where travelers lose memories as tolls. Coral forgets his mother's face; Zephyrine, unsettlingly, gives back one of his own memories in trade. Emotional beat: reluctant intimacy.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Burn Their Maps
chapters.summary: POV Sable, a guild courier. The free cities, learning of the prophecy, begin hunting 'the Taster' themselves—some to crown him, some to kill him. Emotional beat: panic of a world turning Coral into a symbol.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Coral. They reach the underground court of the Soul-Broker, a cathedral of glass roots where sold souls hang like lanterns. Coral finds his own, still warm, still dreaming. Emotional beat: homesickness for a self he never owned.

chapters.title: The Broker's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The Broker explains the original sale: Coral's parents bought their lives with his soul, and only a willing seller can void it—meaning Coral must sell something equal. Emotional beat: fury at inheritance as betrayal.

chapters.title: Zephyrine's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. Flashback-chapter: a century ago Zephyrine witnessed the Delacroix bargain and swore to witness its undoing, which is why he cannot simply take the soul by force. Emotional beat: the god's own chains revealed.

chapters.title: Sable at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Sable. The courier catches up, sent by the surviving guild to help—or to mark Coral for the cities. She chooses help after seeing the hanging souls. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over orders.

chapters.title: What Coral Would Sell
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral inventories what equals a soul: his name, his taste-memory, his future. He begins drafting the contract and finds he cannot write the word 'willing.' Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Usurper Descends
chapters.summary: POV antagonist, Lord Veyra. The usurper's armies reach the mountain, seeking not conquest but the Broker's ledger—every soul-debt in the realm, leverage over everyone alive. Emotional beat: cold ambition meeting older power.

chapters.title: Lanterns Going Out
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Veyra's soldiers breach the court; souls are seized like coin. In the chaos Coral grabs his own lantern-soul and it recognizes him, weeping light. Emotional beat: overwhelming belonging.

chapters.title: The Toll Comes Due
chapters.summary: POV Coral. To escape, Coral pays Zephyrine early—all ninety-one immunities at once. He convulses through every poison he ever swallowed, dying and refusing to die. Emotional beat: survival's cost paid in full.

chapters.title: A Body Made Honest
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable drags the broken, now-mortal Coral out as the mountain court collapses behind them. For the first time he can be killed by a single cup of wine. Emotional beat: tenderness toward fragility.

chapters.title: The Prophecy Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Reading the prophecy again, Coral understands it never named a savior—it named whoever held both soul and ledger, and Veyra now holds the ledger. Emotional beat: clarity sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Veyra's Empty Crown
chapters.summary: POV Veyra. Armed with the ledger, Veyra calls in the realm's debts and finds the debts call back—souls refuse to serve a thief. Emotional beat: corruption devouring itself.

chapters.title: The Last Tasting
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral offers Veyra the one trade that undoes everything: his reclaimed soul for the ledger's destruction, willingly given, breaking the arithmetic of inheritance forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom—he expects to live, changed.

chapters.title: Zephyrine and the Wolf
chapters.summary: POV Zephyrine. The title chapter: freed by Coral's willing gift, Zephyrine reveals he was the first soul ever sold, and Coral's act unchains them both. Together they scatter the ledger's debts to their rightful owners. Emotional beat: release, ancient and new.

chapters.title: Ninety-Two Dishes
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Months later, Coral cooks instead of tasting, mortal and unafraid, keeping a small honest ledger of ordinary things. Zephyrine visits each snowfall. Emotional beat: peace earned, not inherited—an ending that chooses openness over safety.
